src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) (Re Exam ) 2015
s: Which of the following is not responsible for the increase in the biodiversity of an ecosystem?
x: High productivity, intermediate disturbance and greater ecosystem age all raise biodiversity. Fewer trophic levels reduce it, so that is the factor not responsible.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Which of the following is not a type of biodiversity?
x: The three levels of biodiversity are genetic, species and ecosystem diversity; 'population biodiversity' is not a recognised type.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: Biodiversity is valued for
x: Biodiversity preserves ecological processes, maintains hydrological cycles and supports global life-support systems, so all of the above.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains P
s: What is Alpha Diversity?
o: Species biodiversity between two habitats (local communities)
Species biodiversity within a habitat (local community)
x: Alpha diversity is species diversity within one habitat or community. Diversity between habitats is beta, and over a whole region or biome is gamma diversity.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: Out of the recognized species on earth insects constitute approximately about?
x: About 1 million of the roughly 1.8 million described species are insects, so insects make up about half (50%) of recognised species. NCERT says insects are over 70% of animal species, not of all species.

src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP BC Wel
s: Approximately how much percentage of world's species live in tropical rain forests?
x: Tropical rainforests cover under 10% of land but hold about half (often quoted 50%+) of the world's species. 20% and 30% understate it.

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: Cissus Quadrangularis (Nalleru) is used as medicine for
x: Nalleru (Cissus quadrangularis, 'bone setter') is used in traditional medicine for bone health and fracture healing.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: How many quadrats of 20 x 20 square metres can be taken from an area of 20 hectares if the sampling intensity is 1%?
x: 20 ha = 2,00,000 m²; 1% sampling intensity = 2,000 m² to be sampled; one 20 m × 20 m quadrat = 400 m², so 2,000 ÷ 400 = 5 quadrats. 4 would sample only 0.8% of the area.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What is the term used to refer to the population value of a characteristic?
x: A parameter is a numerical characteristic of the whole population (e.g. population mean μ); a statistic is the corresponding value computed from a sample, and an estimate is a statistic's value used to approximate the parameter. Probability is unrelated to this definition.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The hot spots of biodiversity are characterized by
o: Low population, low endemicity and low threat of extinction
Low population, low endemicity and higher threat of extinction
Rich population, high endemicity and low threat of extinction
Rich population, high endemicity and high threat of extinction
x: Biodiversity hotspots have rich species populations, high endemism and a high threat of habitat loss and extinction. (Moved to the hotspots row.)

src: APPSC Endowment Prelims 2023
s: Which of the following is NOT an extinct species?
x: The red panda is endangered but alive (Eastern Himalaya). The dodo, the West African black rhino (2011) and the Chinese river dolphin (baiji, functionally extinct 2006) are extinct.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Read the
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) carefully, and select the correct option.
(A): Parthenium hysterophorus are considered the second largest threat to biodiversity.
(R): Invasive species are a threat to biodiversity.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A).
x:
APPSC key: (A) both true, R explains A. Strictly: 'second largest threat' is said of invasive species as a group; Parthenium is only one of them.
Invasive alien species are the second-biggest cause of biodiversity loss after habitat destruction, and Parthenium (congress grass) is one of India's worst invasive weeds; so A and R are true and R explains A.

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: Which organization publishes data about rare and extinct species?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: The IUCN publishes the Red List and Red Data Book on threatened, rare and extinct species. UNEP and the other options do not.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: The 'Red Data Book' is a document established by the
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: The Red Data Book is compiled by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), which keeps the Red List of threatened species.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Which human activity affects biodiversity the most?
x: Deforestation destroys whole habitats, so it affects biodiversity the most; afforestation and organic farming help it. (Off-topic: biodiversity loss.)

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, Technical Asst. (Hydrog
s: Which of the following National Park is situated in Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
x: Campbell Bay NP (1992) is on Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Dachigam is in J&K, Gir in Gujarat and Guindy in Chennai.

src: APPSC Endowment Paper-I 2023
s: Which of the following lakes is situated between the deltas of the Godavari and Krishna rivers?
x: Kolleru Lake, AP's Ramsar site, lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; Pulicat is on the AP–TN border, Wular in J&K, Vembanad in Kerala.

src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
s: Which of these lakes is in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kolleru Lake is in Andhra Pradesh; Loktak is in Manipur, Vembanad in Kerala and Chilika in Odisha.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: Select the correct match Wild Life Sanctuary areas in Andhra Pradesh
x: Rollapadu Wildlife (Bird) Sanctuary is in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, AP, known for the Great Indian Bustard. (AP protected-area item, moved.)

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s: Which of the following statements regarding the India Rhino Vision (IRV) 2020 is INCORRECT?
o: Its vision was to build a wild population of 3,000 Greater One Horned Rhinos by 2020.
It was launched in partnership with WWF India and the International Rhino Foundation.
It was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
IRV achieved its target of increasing the population of Greater One Horned Rhinos in Assam to 3,000 by 2020.
x: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was adopted in 2005 by the Assam government (with the Bodoland Territorial Council) in partnership with WWF India and the International Rhino Foundation, not launched by MoEFCC. It aimed at 3,000 wild rhinos in 7 PAs of Assam by 2020, a target believed to have been met.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s: Which of the following statements about the Wildlife (Protection) Act (WPA), 1972, is correct?
o: The Act was amended in 2010 to establish the NTCA.
The 2022 amendment to the Act reduced the number of Schedules from six to five.
The 1972 Act covers animal species, not plant species.
The WPA 1972 established the Central Zoo Authority, which regulates the management of zoos in India.
x: The Central Zoo Authority was created under the WPA 1972 by its 1991 amendment, so D is correct. NTCA came in 2006, not 2010. The 2022 amendment cut the schedules to four, not five. The Act also covers plants (Schedule VI, 1991). (WPA item, moved.)

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: Under the Vanam-Manam Programme in total how many trees are proposed to be planted?
x:
the drive's yearly targets changed (2 crore in 2016, 1 crore in 2017, 25 crore in 2018-19) — the 1 crore (10 million) figure is the 2017 target (Hans India, 30 Jun 2017).
For the 2017 Vanam-Manam drive the AP government targeted one crore (10 million) saplings across the State, as part of its goal of 50% green cover by 2029.

src: TSPSC AMVI 2023
s:
Choose the correct option based on the statements below:
Statement I: Deforestation leads to loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services
Statement II: The government of India has established community-based forest management systems to involve local communities in the conservation and management of forest resources.
x: Both are true: deforestation causes loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services, and India has community-based forest management (Joint Forest Management, forest rights) to involve local communities. The printed item had no key.

src: TREI-RB JL & DL (S1) 2023
s: The Chipko movement, began in Uttarakhand demanded
o: Local Communities should have effective control over natural resources like land, water and forests
Prohibition of liquor that spoils household economy
Stopping of economic exploitation of forests by corporates
x: The Chipko villagers demanded that no forest-exploitation contracts be given to outsiders and that local communities have effective control over natural resources like land, water and forests (NCERT Class XII Politics in India since Independence).

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit
s:
A: Global warming is a gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth's lower atmosphere.
R: Global warming is a result of the increase in greenhouse gases since the industrial revolution.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Global warming is the gradual rise in the average temperature of the lower atmosphere, and it is caused by the rise in greenhouse gases since the Industrial Revolution, so R explains A. (Moved to climate change.)

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: As per recent data, what is the average level of Carbon Dioxide in atmosphere in India (choose nearest figure)?
x: Atmospheric CO2 crossed 400 ppm in 2015-16 and is about 420+ ppm now, so 400 ppm is the nearest figure.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: A small change in temperature of the earth does not cause?
o: Starvation of all plants and animals
Melting of ice at the poles
Flooding in some places and drought in other places
x: A small rise in Earth's temperature melts polar ice, raises seas and brings floods and droughts. It would not starve all plants and animals. (Off-topic: climate change.)

src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC, Tribal Welfare Officers 2017
s: Global warming would make the Indian Monsoon
o: It is too early to predict
x: Global warming is expected to make the Indian monsoon more erratic and extreme (devastating and unpredictable).

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: What is the main aim of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change?
o: To limit global temperature rise to well below 2° C
x: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: The Paris Climate Agreement (2015) mainly aims to
o: Limit global temperature rise to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels
Increase fossil fuel production for energy security
x: Paris (2015) aims to keep the temperature rise well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.

src: TSPSC Group-IV Paper-I 2023
s:
Which is/are correct about the goal/goals of Paris Climate Agreement?

A. To hold "the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels".

B. To pursue efforts "to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels".
x: Both are Paris goals: well below 2°C (A) and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C (B).

src: AE (Subordinate Services) Mains 2017
s: In the COP 21 convention held at Paris, it was proposed to limit the level of global warming to
o: 3 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
1 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
2 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
4 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
x: COP21 Paris set the limit at 2°C above pre-industrial levels (well below 2°C, aiming for 1.5°C).

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: Which of the following was the first country to declare the climate emergency?
x: The UK Parliament was the first national parliament to declare a climate emergency, on 1 May 2019.

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit
s:
A: A UN Conference on Climate Change, held in Kyoto, Japan, in 1997 called for reductions in emissions of greenhouse gases by industrialised nations.
R: Montreal Protocol banned the use of chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) compounds, as well as other ozone-depleting chemicals such as carbon tetrachloride, trichloroethane (also known as methyl chloroform), and bromine compounds are known as halons.
o: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true: Kyoto (1997) set emission cuts for industrialised nations, and the Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs, halons and other ozone-depleting substances. R is about ozone, not greenhouse-gas cuts, so it does not explain A. (Moved to climate initiatives.)

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Kyoto Protocol deals with
x: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) under the UNFCCC sets binding greenhouse-gas cuts for developed countries, so it deals with climate change. Ozone depletion is the Montreal Protocol; biodiversity is the CBD.

src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary/Mahil
s: The Principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities is specially focused on
x: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (and Respective Capabilities) is the core equity principle of the UNFCCC climate regime: developed countries take the lead in cutting emissions. India invokes it in climate talks.

src: TREI-RB Lecturers 2023
s: Where was the 2022 United Nations Climate Change Conference, referred as COP-27 held in November, 2022?
x: COP27 (November 2022) was held at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. COP28 was in Dubai (UAE) and COP26 in Glasgow (UK).

src: Polytechnic Lecturers 2020
s: 'Kyoto Protocol', which was adopted in 1997, is associated with:
x: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, deals with climate change: binding greenhouse-gas cuts for developed countries. It is not about noise, population or general air pollution.

src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
s: Where is the head quarters of International Solar Alliance, an Intergovernmental Organization to promote solar energy is located?
x: The International Solar Alliance, launched by India and France at COP21 (2015), is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana. It is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: As per recent study by researchers of University of Maryland, India's emissions of the air pollutant sulphur dioxide increased by approximately how much percent since 2007 (choose nearest figure)?
x: The 2017 University of Maryland-led study (Scientific Reports, with NASA OMI satellite data) found India's SO2 emissions up about 50% since 2007 while China's fell about 75%. So 50 percent, not 75 or 100.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: As per the WHO report released in May, 2016, which is the worst city in India in terms of air pollution?
x: The WHO's May 2016 urban air-quality database ranked Gwalior the most polluted Indian city (2nd in the world after Zabol, Iran), ahead of Allahabad, Patna and Raipur.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which of the following is the principal cause of acid rain?
x: Acid rain is caused mainly by high SO2 (with NOx) that forms sulphuric and nitric acids; ozone depletion, UV-B and GHGs are not its cause.

src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
s:
Which of the following is/are the methods to control air pollution?
(i) Setting up of cheaper and faster public transportation systems with better connectivity.
(ii) Devising rules to ensure pooling of private transport.
(iii) Setting up sound-proof infrastructure in the hospitals.
x: Cheaper, faster public transport and pooling of private vehicles cut vehicle emissions; sound-proofing hospitals addresses noise, not air pollution, so (i) and (ii).

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
s: According to reports of Central Pollution Control Board of India, what was the average air quality index (AQI) of Delhi in 2021?
x: Printed key: 144. Caution: CAQM/CPCB-based reports give Delhi's 2021 daily-average AQI as about 209 for the whole year, so the 144 figure may refer to a part of the year or a different metric. (AQI item, moved.)

src: UPSC Civils Prelims 2021
s:
Magnetite particles, suspected to cause neurodegenerative problems are generated as environmental pollutants from which of the following?

1. Brakes of motor vehicles

2. Engines of motor vehicles

3. Microwave stoves within homes

4. Power plants

5. Telephone lines
Select the correct answer using the code given below
x: Magnetite comes from vehicle brakes, vehicle engines and coal-fired power plants (1, 2, 4); there is no evidence for microwave stoves or telephone lines.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: Out of the given below acids, which one is prominently found in acid rain?
x: SO2 from burning coal and oil forms sulphuric acid, the main acid of acid rain; NOx adds nitric acid. Hydrochloric, formic and acetic acids are minor or absent.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: According to Ministry of Environment and Forest, Government of India, between 2006 to 2015 in the lives lost due to the Air pollution, which of the following states had the highest deaths?
x: The MoEF reply put acute respiratory infection deaths in 2006-2015 at 35,616, with West Bengal the highest, followed by Andhra Pradesh. Off-topic (environment).

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Which is a measure to control air pollution?
x: Switching vehicles to CNG, a cleaner fuel, cuts air pollution; deforestation, more vehicles and burning plastic all worsen it.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
s: Which of the following is most affected by acid rains?
x: Acid rain lowers the pH of poorly buffered lakes and streams, so fish (and the shrimps, snails and mussels they feed on) decline or are eliminated; its effects on birds and mammals are indirect and hard to document. Off-topic (air pollution), moved.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: According to World Health Organization, how much percentage of the world's population was living in places where the WHO air quality guidelines levels were not met in 2019?
x: WHO reported (2022 database update) that 99% of the world's population in 2019 lived where its air-quality guideline levels were not met.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Acid rain occurs when precipitation becomes more acidic than usual, with a pH below 5.6.
Reason (R): Nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) are formed during high-temperature combustion reactions, which later react with water to form nitric acid (HNO3), contributing to acid rain.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
x: Rain with pH below 5.6 is acid rain; NOx from high-temperature combustion forms nitric acid in the air, which is one cause of acid rain, so R explains A.

src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
s: According to recent study of IIT, Mumbai what is the approximate cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015?
x: An IIT Bombay study put the economic cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015 at about Rs 70,000 crore. Pollution item, moved.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s: Which was the first State/UT to implement the Odd-Even Scheme to combat air pollution?
x: Delhi first ran the odd-even road-rationing scheme in January 2016 to fight air pollution. Off-topic (pollution), moved.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: Which of the following is not a way of reducing air pollution?
o: Going fast to the destination in automobile
Travelling by Bus instead of Car
Using diesel car instead of petrol car
x:
No printed key. Strictly, 'going fast to the destination' is not a way of reducing pollution either (fuel use rises at high speed); the diesel option is keyed as the standard textbook point.
Diesel cars emit more NOx and particulates than petrol cars, so switching to diesel does not reduce air pollution; natural gas vehicles and buses instead of cars do.

src: U.P.U.D.A/L.D.A. (Pre) 2013
s: Which one of the following is known for cleaning a polluted environment?
x: Rain washes particles and soluble gases out of the air (wet deposition), so it cleans a polluted atmosphere. (Moved to 5:99.)

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: Eutrophication is a
at: Process of nutrient accumulation in the water bodies
x: Eutrophication is the enrichment of water bodies with nutrients (N, P), which causes algal blooms that deplete oxygen and kill aquatic life.

src: TSPSC Polytechnic Lecturer 06-09-2023
s: IISER Pune developed macro/microporous ionic organic framework in 2023 which can
x: IISER Pune (2023) made a macro/microporous ionic organic framework that rapidly traps toxic oxo-anion pollutants (e.g. chromate, arsenate) from water.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: How can improper waste management, especially biomedical and e-waste, indirectly contribute to deforestation and biodiversity loss?
o: By providing organic fertilizers that help forest regeneration
By releasing toxic substances into soil and water, damaging ecosystems and forcing land-use changes like deforestation
By reducing industrial pollution and improving ecosystem balance
By increasing green cover through waste-to-energy plants in forests
x: Improperly managed biomedical and e-waste releases toxic substances into soil and water, damaging ecosystems and pushing land-use change. The other options describe benefits, not harm.

src: ASO Mains 2017
s: As per Indian State of Forest Report (ISFR)-2015, what is the total carbon stock in forests of India?
x: ISFR 2015 put the carbon stock of India's forests at 7,044 million tonnes. (Moved to 5:104.)

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
s: Which Agency in India ensures implementation of fire cracker safety standards?
x: The Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO, under DPIIT) licenses fireworks and enforces their safety standards. (Moved to 5:105.)

src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
s: Which of the following is not a reason for increasing vulnerability to disasters?
o: Blind faith in beliefs and customs
x: Lack of resources, low awareness and blind faith raise vulnerability to disasters; spread of irrigation reduces drought vulnerability and is not a cause.

src: APPSC Asst. Hydrologist and other posts 2017
s: Which weapon of biological disaster was used by the European colonizers of America to wipe out native red Indians?
x: At Fort Pitt (1763) the British gave Native Americans 'two Blankets and an Handkerchief out of the Small Pox Hospital' – smallpox-laden cloth, so (a). Jaundice, anthrax and flu are wrong.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Land slides occur mostly in ______ areas.
x: Landslides occur mostly in hilly and mountainous areas with steep slopes (Himalayas, Western Ghats).

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer 2012
s: Main objective of First Aid is
o: To prevent victim's condition from worsening
x: First aid aims to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening and promote recovery - all the above (the three Ps).

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
s: The outcome of hazard mapping is
o: Segregation of different types of hazards
x: Hazard mapping shows where hazards occur and so identifies vulnerable areas; evacuation plans and fund allocation are later uses of the map.

src: APPSC AEE (Asst. Executive Engineer) 2023
s: Which of the following is a natural factor which makes the country prone to various forms of disasters?
x: Extreme weather (cyclones, floods, droughts) is a natural factor; unscientific development, population pressure and unplanned urbanisation are human-made.

src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
s: What does the colour black in triage refer to?
x: In START triage, black means the casualty is dead or expectant (not expected to survive), so only comfort care such as pain relief is given. Red is life-threatening, yellow serious, green minor.

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer & Analyst Grade-II (A
s: Which of the following is the least effective way to prepare for a hurricane?
o: Leaving valuables in a low-lying area
x: Hurricanes (tropical cyclones) bring storm surge and flooding that hit low-lying areas first, so leaving valuables there is the least effective step - they should be moved to higher, safer places. Securing outdoor furniture, boarding up windows and a family communication plan are all standard preparedness measures.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Which of the following best describes the role of biotechnology in environmental sustainability?
o: Using genetically modified microbes and plants to reduce pollution and conserve natural resources
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides
x: Biotechnology serves environmental sustainability by using GM microbes and plants for bioremediation and resource saving. More agrochemicals, deforestation or extra plastics do the opposite. (Moved to 5:108.)

src: UPSC Civils Prelims 2023
s: 'Aerial metagenomics' best refers to which one of the following situations?
o: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
Understanding the genetic makeup of avian species of a habitat
Using air-borne devices to collect blood samples from moving animals
Sending drones to inaccessible areas to collect plant and animal samples from land surfaces and water bodies
x: Aerial metagenomics means collecting DNA from the air of a habitat in one go and sequencing it to identify the species present. It does not need blood samples, drones or a study of birds only.

src: TREI-RB Lecturers 2023
s:
Identify the correct statements relating to 'IndiGau'

A. Second largest cattle chip of the world

B. It is developed for the conservation of pure varieties of indigenous cattle breeds

C. India's first Cattle Genomic Chip
x: IndiGau (NIAB Hyderabad, Aug 2021) is India's first cattle genomic chip, made for conserving pure indigenous breeds such as Gir, Kankrej, Sahiwal and Ongole; the government called it the world's largest cattle chip, not the second largest, so A is wrong.

src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
s: The Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) facility was inaugurated in which city?
x: The Next Generation Sequencing facility was inaugurated at CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad, by Union S&T Minister Harsh Vardhan in July 2019; it can sequence up to 30 human genomes a day.

src: TSPSC Tutors in Medical Education, Dental Asst Surgeon, Civi
s:
Consider the following in relation to a new artificial womb technology:

A. It uses ex-vivo uterine environment therapy

B. It aims to prevent the severe morbidity suffered by premature infants

C. It uses amniotic fluid bath combined with an artificial placenta

D. It has been successfully used on human bodies at the Tohoku University Hospital, Japan
Select the right answer:
x: EVE (ex-vivo uterine environment) therapy uses an amniotic-fluid bath with an artificial placenta to save extremely premature infants (A, B, C true); it was tested on lambs, not yet on humans, so D is false.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
s: Scientists of which institute have developed a simple paper kit that can test freshness of milk and tell how well it has been pasteurized?
x: Researchers of IIT Guwahati developed a simple paper kit that shows milk freshness and how well it was pasteurised.

src: Miscellaneous Exams
s:
With reference to 'Optogenetics' which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Optogenetics is a relatively new field of biotechnology.

2. It gives researchers the ability to transform brain activity into light and light into brain activity.

3. It will serve as an interface through which computers can become part of our brain, and through which our art of our brains could directly interface with each other.

4. It is the practice of stimulating biased inheritance of particular genes to alter entire populations.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
x: Optogenetics is a new field that uses light-sensitive proteins to turn light into neural activity and to read activity as light (1, 2). Statement 4 describes a gene drive, so the printed key '1, 2 and 4' is wrong, and statement 3 is only a speculative possibility (WEF frames it as a question), so 1 and 2 only.

src: TSPSC Group-II Paper-I 2016
s: Though officially not recognised at first, Subash Mukhopadhyaya created India's first and world's second Test Tube baby on 3rd October, 1978. What is the name of the baby?
x: Kanupriya Agarwal, nicknamed Durga, born in Kolkata on 3 October 1978 through Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyay's work, was India's first (and the world's second) IVF baby, after Louise Brown (UK, July 1978).

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: In which district, A.P government is developing Bio-Technology Hub?
x: The printed answer is Visakhapatnam, where the AP government planned its biotechnology hub/park.

src: TSPSC Tutors in Medical Education, Dental Asst Surgeon, Civi
s: Scientists from the following organization have successfully created an implanted bio-artificial Pancreas.
x: IIT Guwahati researchers created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas (3D-printed, insulin-secreting) for diabetes.

src: TSPSC Gurukulam JL, DL, Language Pandits 2017
s: From whom among the following scientists have successfully created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas?
x: IIT Guwahati researchers created an implantable bio-artificial pancreas (3D-printed, insulin-secreting) for diabetes.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The first ever genome sequencing of the Jamun tree (Syzygium cumini) was completed by the researchers of
o: National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) New Delhi
Jawaharlal Nehru Center for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bangalore
Indian Institute of Science Educational and Research (IISER), Bhopal
x: Researchers at IISER Bhopal completed the first genome sequencing of the jamun tree (Syzygium cumini) in 2023.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: If progeny is produced by crossing two types of pea plants i.e. Tall and Short (Tall being the dominant trait), then in the first generation what would be the percentage of Tall plants?

src: APPSC Polytechnic Colleges (Engineering & Non-Engineering) G
s: Select the correct statement about in vitro fertilisation (IVF).
o: In vitro fertilisation (IVF) is a type of assisted cardiac technology (ART).
In vitro fertilisation (IVF) sperm and an egg are fertilised inside the human body.
IVF is a complex process that involves retrieving eggs from ovaries and manually combining them with sperm in a lab for fertilisation.
Several days after fertilisation, the fertilised egg (now called an embryo) is placed inside the testis of the male.
x: IVF retrieves eggs from the ovaries and fertilises them with sperm in a laboratory, outside the body; the embryo is then transferred into the woman's uterus (not into a testis). It is an assisted reproductive technology (ART), not 'assisted cardiac technology', and fertilisation does not happen inside the body.
